definitions.explanation: the activity of removing unwanted plants (weeds) from a garden or field

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{草取|くさと}りは{腰|こし}が{痛|いた}くなる。
examples.english: Weeding the garden makes my back hurt.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{草取|くさと}りが{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Weeding is hard work in summer.

examples.japanese: {畑|はたけ}の{草取|くさと}りを{手伝|てつだ}った。
examples.english: I helped with weeding the field.

notes:
{草取|くさと}り refers to the chore of pulling weeds from a garden, yard, or field. A very common activity in Japanese households, especially during the warm months when weeds grow rapidly.

FORMS:
{草|くさ} (grass/weeds) + {取|と}り (taking/removing, from {取|と}る).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {草取|くさと}りをする: to do weeding
- {庭|にわ}の{草取|くさと}り: weeding the garden
- {畑|はたけ}の{草取|くさと}り: weeding the field
- {草取|くさと}り{鎌|がま}: weeding sickle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {草取|くさと}り: weeding (standard)
- {草|くさ}むしり: weeding (more colloquial — from むしる, to pluck)
- {除草|じょそう}: weeding/herbicide application (formal/technical)

RELATED GARDENING CHORES:
- {芝刈|しばか}り: lawn mowing
- {水|みず}やり: watering
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}かき: raking fallen leaves
- {剪定|せんてい}: pruning
